explanation: The one who served in the earthly sanctuary and offered sacrifices for sins, a role Jesus took on with an eternal and perfect sacrifice.
An agreement between God and humanity; this chapter contrasts the old covenant (Mosaic law) with the new and better covenant in Christ.
The holy place where God's presence dwelt, either the earthly temple building or heaven where Jesus now serves as our High Priest.
Literally "law" or "instruction"; here it often refers to the written commands and rituals in the Old Testament that were replaced by God's will written on the heart.
The inner person, thoughts, and will; in the new covenant, God promises to write His law directly there instead of on stone tablets.
The concept that all will know the Lord from the least to the greatest through a personal relationship rather than merely through external teaching or rituals.
Actions that break God's will; in the new covenant, God promises no longer to remember people's sins and transgressions after they are forgiven.
